title: How to run an app on a physical iPhone in Xcode on Mac: complete guide
metaTitle: How to run an app on a physical iPhone in Xcode on Mac
description: Learn how to run an app on a physical iPhone in Xcode on Mac. Follow our step-by-step guide to connect, sign, and launch your app on real hardware today.

intro: To run an app on a physical iPhone in Xcode on Mac, you must connect your device via USB and select it as the run destination in the top toolbar. Once selected, ensure your signing team is configured in the project settings before pressing the run button.
tldr: Connect your iPhone to your Mac using a reliable USB cable.
Trust the computer on your iPhone when prompted.
Select your iPhone from the device picker in the Xcode toolbar.
Configure your team in the Signing & Capabilities tab.
Enable Developer Mode in your iPhone Settings if required.
Press Command + R to build and run your application.

blocks.text: Preparing your environment for physical device testing

Before you can run an app on a physical iPhone in Xcode on Mac, you need to ensure your development environment is ready. Xcode 27 requires macOS Tahoe 26.6 or later. Ensure your Mac is running this version to avoid compatibility issues. Always use an Apple certified cable or a high quality third party alternative to ensure stable data transfer during the build process.
Connecting your device and establishing trust

The first step is a physical connection. Plug your iPhone into your Mac. Your iPhone will display an alert asking if you trust this computer. Tap Trust and enter your device passcode. This creates a secure pairing record. Without this, Xcode cannot communicate with the device. If the device does not appear in Xcode, unplug it, wait five seconds, and reconnect it.

Xcode requires a valid signature to install apps on physical hardware. Open your project in the Project Navigator. Click on your project file at the top of the list. Navigate to the Signing & Capabilities tab. Select your development team from the Team dropdown menu. If you do not have a team, log in to your Apple ID in Xcode Settings > Accounts. Once signed in, Xcode automatically manages the provisioning profiles required for testing.
Enabling Developer Mode on your iPhone

Modern iOS versions require you to manually enable Developer Mode. Go to Settings on your iPhone. Navigate to Privacy & Security. Scroll down to the bottom to find Developer Mode. Toggle the switch to on. Your iPhone will prompt you to restart the device. This step is mandatory for running code directly from Xcode. You only need to do this once per device.
Selecting your target and running the app

Once the device is connected and Developer Mode is active, look at the top toolbar in Xcode. You will see a device selector menu. Click this menu and choose your physical iPhone from the list. If it is not visible, check that the device is unlocked and connected. Press Command + R to build and install your app. Xcode will compile the code and launch the app on your phone.

blocks.text: Testing on a simulator is fast, but it does not replicate real world conditions. Physical devices have different thermal characteristics, camera performance, and GPS accuracy. You should perform final testing on the actual hardware your users own. This helps identify performance bottlenecks that do not appear in the simulator. It also allows you to test interactions like haptic feedback and physical button presses.

faq.question: Do I need a paid developer account to run apps on my iPhone?
faq.answer: No. You can run apps on your own devices using a free Apple ID. You only need a paid account to distribute apps on the App Store.

faq.question: Can I run my app wirelessly?
faq.answer: Yes. Once you have paired your device via cable, you can enable wireless debugging in the Devices and Simulators window.

faq.question: How often should I clean my build folder?
faq.answer: If you encounter strange build errors that do not make sense, cleaning the build folder is a good first step to clear out stale cache files.

troubleshooting.problem: Device does not appear in Xcode
troubleshooting.fix: Ensure the cable is connected and the device is unlocked.
Ensure you are on the latest iOS version.
Clean your build folder using Shift + Command + K.
